name: Common Ground

scoring.report_note: Report group-level deltas only. Never rank groups or individuals — the hunt measures the group's question-asking habits, not talent.

description: Two-minute pre/post measure for the Common Ground icebreaker. Scores at group level: how did curiosity, second questions, listening and safety to disagree change across the hunt?

instructions.pre: Before groups form. Each participant answers alone, about their own last week at work — not about the exercise.
instructions.post: Immediately after the debrief. Same items, now answered about the hunt just completed, as a group.

items.pre_text: After someone answers me, I ask one more question.
items.post_text: During the hunt, we asked a second question after easy answers.

items.pre_text: I know at least one non-work fact about each of my closest colleagues.
items.post_text: The hunt uncovered non-obvious facts about people I thought I knew.

items.pre_text: I take the first workable answer and move on.
items.post_text: We camped on 1-point grounds until the scoring pushed us deeper.

items.pre_text: I can repeat the last thing a quiet colleague said in a meeting.
items.post_text: The quietest member's contribution made it onto our card.

items.pre_text: I say 'actually, that's not true for me' when a group claim misses me.
items.post_text: When a ground didn't hold for someone, they said so — and the group thanked them.

items.pre_text: I feel I belong on my current team.
items.post_text: Finding shared ground changed how belonging feels for this group.

report.title: Common Ground — group curiosity delta
sections: One suggested question habit per group, derived from the largest positive delta
